population_banner:
POPULATION: this projection covers 172 declared ET-CC members and 120
declared in-population OC checks. That is the slice adjudicated so far,
and it is NOT the whole conformance picture: the full comparison is 281
ET-CC members and 173 in-denominator OC checks, of which 109 members and
53 checks are not_yet_adjudicated -- a third state, distinct from bucket
1 -- owned by the tickets the crosswalk's own `outside_the_population`
block names. A further 0 checks carry an edge without being declared by
any file, so they are counted in neither.

A count of zero in this view means zero WITHIN THAT SLICE. It does not
mean zero in the suite. As the declared population grows this projection
re-runs and fills.

EVERY FIGURE ABOVE IS INTERPOLATED from the crosswalk being projected;
none is written here. The [population_statement] guard refuses a
population figure that is not.
predicate: `cells` where the stored `bucket` == "4b". Universe: the crosswalk's edges.

rows.claim: a removed `ping` over HTTP yields JSON-RPC error -32601
rows.evidence: streamable_http_stateless_test.exs:90 — `assert error(post(opts(), rpc("ping", %{})))["code"] == -32_601`, which is the code the check requires. The HTTP status is not asserted.
rows.note: INHERITED, NOT NEWLY ADJUDICATED: this is match-relation.md §4's worked edge record, published by A3 with these axes and this shape. A3 §1 assigns the per-claim decomposition of this member to C1; §4 then performs it. C1a records it rather than re-deciding it.
oc_key: If the server does not implement the removed RPC method 'ping', it MUST respond with 404 Not Found and a JSON-RPC error with code -32601 (Method not found).

rows.claim: a removed `logging/setLevel` over HTTP yields JSON-RPC error -32601
rows.evidence: streamable_http_stateless_test.exs:91 — `assert error(post(opts(), rpc("logging/setLevel", %{"level" => "info"})))["code"] == -32_601`. Same shape as the ping claim, a different removed method.
rows.note: The third of A3 §1's three edges for this member.
oc_key: If the server does not implement the removed RPC method 'logging/setLevel', it MUST respond with 404 Not Found and a JSON-RPC error with code -32601 (Method not found).

rows.claim: a dispatched `ping` is answered with -32601 method-not-found
rows.evidence: dispatch_test.exs:88-95 — `assert ping_resp["error"]["code"] == -32_601`. The OC axis `i?.error?.code!==-32601` is `fail_when_true`, so -32601 is the passing direction and our claim agrees. The check is nonetheless RED, and its message says why: `Expected HTTP 404 and code -32601 for removed methods, got HTTP 200 and code -32601` — the code half is satisfied and the status half is not. the ET claim is asserted at `MCP.Server.Dispatch`, BELOW the transport — the unit never constructs an HTTP response, so nothing in it has an HTTP status as its subject and the axis is silent by `how_a_silent_axis_was_decided`'s rule rather than by omission.

rows.claim: a deployment that cannot serve subscriptions/listen answers it with -32601, never a silent black hole
rows.evidence: subscriptions_dispatch_test.exs:368-373 — `json_mode = config(streaming: false)`, then `Dispatch.dispatch(listen_request(%{"toolsListChanged" => true}), ctx(), json_mode)` and `assert error["code"] == -32_601`. The OC check is the GENERIC unimplemented-method row, not one of the five removed-method rows, and a deployment that does not implement `subscriptions/listen` is exactly its case. Asserted below the transport, so the status axis is silent.
